title: The Authority of Scripture
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: The authority of Scripture means that God’s written Word is the final standard for truth, doctrine, obedience, correction, worship, and discipleship. Because Scripture is breathed out by God, it carries His authority and must be received, trusted, obeyed, and taught as His Word.
summary: The authority of Scripture means that God’s written Word is the final standard for truth, doctrine, obedience, correction, worship, and discipleship. Because Scripture is breathed out by God, it carries His authority and must be received, trusted, obeyed, and taught as His Word.
christFocus: Jesus Christ submitted to, fulfilled, quoted, obeyed, and upheld the Scriptures. He resisted temptation with the written Word, prayed that God’s people would be sanctified by the truth, and showed that Scripture ultimately bears witness to Him. To honor Christ rightly, believers must also honor the Word He trusted, fulfilled, and proclaimed.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Scripture is not merely a collection of religious writings, human reflections, moral lessons, or ancient wisdom. The Bible is the written Word of God, given through human authors as they were carried along by the Holy Spirit. Because God is the source of Scripture, its authority does not depend on culture, popularity, tradition, personal feelings, or human approval.

The authority of Scripture means God has the right to define truth, expose sin, correct error, command obedience, reveal salvation, and shape the life of His people. Scripture teaches what is true, shows what is wrong, corrects what has gone astray, and trains believers in righteousness. God has not left His people to guess who He is, what salvation means, or how they should live.

Jesus Himself treated Scripture as authoritative. When tempted, He answered with the written Word. When teaching, He appealed to Scripture as truth. When fulfilling His mission, He showed that God’s Word cannot fail. The authority of Scripture is not opposed to Christ; it leads us to Christ, reveals Christ, and teaches us to follow Christ faithfully.

When Scripture is rejected, ignored, twisted, or placed beneath human opinion, God’s people lose their foundation. But when Scripture is received as God’s Word, believers are corrected, strengthened, sanctified, equipped, and anchored in truth. The church must never stand above Scripture as judge; the church must stand under Scripture as servant.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
People are surrounded by competing voices: culture, emotion, pain, fear, tradition, politics, false teaching, personal experience, and spiritual deception. Without the authority of Scripture, truth becomes whatever seems right in the moment. The wounded may be misled by feelings, the proud may justify sin, the confused may follow error, and the church may drift from Christ while still using religious language.

The authority of Scripture protects God’s people from building their lives on unstable ground. It gives the broken a trustworthy word, the tempted a firm weapon, the suffering a sure promise, the teacher a faithful standard, and the church a foundation that does not change. God’s Word stands when human opinions fade, and it speaks with authority because the God who gave it is true.

studySections.heading: Discipleship & Application
studySections.content: Come under Scripture with humility, faith, and obedience. Do not use the Bible merely to support what you already want to believe; let God’s Word search you, correct you, comfort you, teach you, and command you. When making decisions, teaching others, facing temptation, confronting sin, or seeking hope, return to Scripture as the final authority. Trust that the Word of God is not given to harm you, but to lead you into truth, maturity, freedom, and faithfulness to Christ.
